mechanism: Use the true strip-width edge and equal-width turn base as a blue source/receiver pair. Compare the red x-scoped straight edge against the red 45-degree turn diagonal. The predeclared error substitutes the turn diagonal 4sqrt(2) for the requested exposed rectangle length x, choosing E.
primary_unique_math_proof: Let y be the exposed height of rectangle Q. Both rectangles have strip width 4, so P=4x and Q=4y. The 45-degree fold turns the strip by 90 degrees, and the transition consumes exactly one width 4 along the original 13 cm strip, giving x+4+y=13. P=2Q gives x=2y, hence 3y=9, y=3 and x=6 uniquely, choice C. The fold diagonal is 4sqrt(2), a different segment from x. These conclusions use the printed width, strip length, fold angle and P=2Q, not display lengths measured from pixels.

human_semantics: No image transformation option is being selected: the choices are numeric lengths. Literal ink on these fixed edges leaves every physical length, strip boundary and the single fold unchanged. Blue marks two true widths. Red groups two visibly different measurements for comparison; common color adds no numerical equality condition. The existing x dimension still spans only P; P,Q,45 degrees and all original solid/dashed lines remain legible. No area paint, new fold, new piece, partition, length label, arrow or false equality is introduced.
